transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Green (Redwood SE), Jia Liu (Redwood CSM), Ava Torres (LumenCloud ML Eng), Rohit Patel (LumenCloud Infra Lead), Sofia Marin (LumenCloud PM)

Auto-summary (brief): quick pass on numbers, a few regression cases to triage, agree next steps for on-prem test and fallback routing.

[00:00] Lena (AE): all right folks, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, and then Marcus will run us through the latest quant results.
[00:12] Ava: hey, thanks. we pushed a couple more evaluation batches last night so hoping to get clarity on the long-tail.
[00:20] Marcus (SE): yeah i'll share screen in a sec; caveat first — some of the FP8 runs were flaky on the nv link so numbers are slightly noisy.
[01:05] Marcus: ok so slide one, aggregated token throughput: FP8 median latency dropped 28% versus fp16 baseline, INT8 was 24% improvement, cpu-side overheads creep in a bit for small seq lengths.
[01:48] Rohit: when you say "fp16 baseline" is that our current onboard model or the open checkpoint?
[01:55] Marcus: it's the open checkpoint we brought in — same weights, no extra distillation. should be representative.
[02:22] Sofia: can you show the quality delta matrix again? the regen rate & exact-match stuff?
[02:30] Marcus: sure, hold on — here's the confusion matrix. noteworthy: INT8's average BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics are within 1.2% on the microbenchmarks but we see spikes on some code-gen and long-context summarization prompts.
[03:10] Ava: yep that's what we saw in our user tests — short text is fine, but prompts longer than ~1k tokens had hallucination uptick with INT8.
[03:28] Marcus: right, and importantly FP8, when it runs clean, tends to keep quality closer to baseline but with higher instability probability — random early exits or NaNs in 0.3% of calls on one kernel. we suspect kernel pathing on that hardware combo.
[04:05] Lena: can you clarify "instability" — is that infra level crash or soft hallucination change?
[04:12] Marcus: infra-level — model compute errors. sometimes fused matmul path returns an inf, triggers failover. we caught it in our logs; auto-fallback to fp16 worked but that adds background latency.
[04:42] Rohit: if fallback triggers, do you route to another model variant or just re-run on fp16? what's the expected SLA hit?
[04:51] Marcus: good q. current pilot config: if a compute error detected, the runtime can automatically switch to a compatible variant (e.g., fp16 variant) or to another region. Practically that means a single-call latency spike of 200-800 ms depending on cold kv cache.
[05:18] Jia (CSM): would be great to quantify that to give product metrics for the client-facing SLOs.
[05:25] Marcus: agreed, i'll annotate the logs for tail latency percentiles tied to fallback events in next run.
[06:00] Ava: real quick — are these fallback logs exposed in the Console? we want to attach to our internal monitoring.
[06:08] Lena: yes, we can expose token-level and route-level traces; Jia will set up a dashboard link.
[06:15] Jia: noted — i'll create an initial dashboard and share the URL.
[06:25] Marcus: moving on to the perceptual quality tests: we ran 2000 synthetic prompts, the delta for INT8 is median 0.6% quality loss but 12 outlier cases. FP8 has median 0.3% loss but 40 outliers due to kernel instability.
[07:05] Rohit: what's an "outlier" defined as?
[07:08] Marcus: where the judgement score drops by more than 5 points on our rubric — in practice these are multi-step math, code, and legalese compression prompts.
[07:30] Ava: interestingly, a lot of our production traffic is short queries, so the median is reassuring — but those outliers are our SLAs.
[07:45] Lena: ok let's talk risk tolerance: do we accept INT8 with fallback path for now and tune, or hold for FP8 once kernel fixes are upstream?
[07:58] Sofia: from product perspective, must keep error-free behavior for customers. we'd accept minor latency spikes but not increased hallucinations on contracts or code.
[08:18] Marcus: operationally, INT8 + deterministic fallback to fp16 seems safest. It gives the cost wins and predictable fallback with small latency penalty. FP8 could be promoted after kernel patches — ramp carefully.
[08:44] Rohit: what's the unit-cost delta we should expect for INT8 v fp16?
[08:50] Lena: rough numbers: INT8 reduces per-token runtime cost ~25-30%, FP8 about 32-35 when stable; but FP8 instability causes higher tail costs. i'll send the precise delta in the updated pricing sheet.
[09:15] Ava: can we get numbers per workload split? i.e., conversational vs codegen vs embeddings?
[09:22] Marcus: yes, i'll slice the regression by prompt-class and share.
[09:30] Marcus: next — we did a KV cache hit-rate experiment. with their prefix caching, the warm cache helps a lot; fallback to fp16 causes miss/refill and that's where the 200-800 ms tail shows up.
[10:05] Rohit: what about batching? can we batch the fallback attempts to amortize overhead?
[10:12] Marcus: not for single interactive calls; batching helps throughput but hurts latency. for async jobs we can batch.
[10:35] Ava: a few noisy ASR items: we saw tokenization differences between our tokenizer and Redwood's loader leading to off-by-one alignment in some regen checks.
[10:46] Marcus: yep we noticed mismatch — our suggestion is to pin the tokenizer version and provide a small shim; we'll share a repro script.
[11:10] Lena: moving to on-prem checklist — Rohit, you had asked about VPC/air-gap and KMS. can you summarize constraints?
[11:20] Rohit: yep we need an air-gapped option; no egress to public internet, KMS via our HSM with strict key rotation policy, and audit logs retained for seven years. also need RBAC integration with our SSO (SAML).
[11:40] Jia: Redwood Private supports KMS integration and on-prem package, but we need the exact KMS endpoints and HSM compatibility test vectors.
[11:50] Rohit: we'll share the HSM vendor doc and a sample key wrap test.
[12:05] Marcus: to run FP8 kernels on your infra, we need to validate driver+cuda combinations; FP8 instability seems correlated with certain driver combos. we'll give you the validated matrix but we recommend dedicating a test node.
[12:28] Ava: what's the plan for canary / rollouts for the pilot? we don't want to break prod.
[12:35] Marcus: recommended plan: start with 5% traffic on INT8 with strict quality monitoring and immediate rollback on regression, then 20% if stable, etc. for FP8 we'd do internal canary first.
[12:55] Lena: add to that automated evals on prompt-sets that you care about — we'll hook them up so canary passes must meet thresholds.
[13:05] Sofia: what are the trigger thresholds? e.g., 2% drop in judgement score for 5-minute window?
[13:12] Marcus: we suggest 1% median and 3% for P95 over baseline for critical prompts, but we'll align to your risk appetite.
[13:35] Ava: back to the regression cases — can we capture concrete examples live?
[13:40] Marcus: yes i'll pull a couple. this first one is a code-gen prompt where INT8 returns missing import lines intermittently.
[14:02] Ava: i can reproduce that locally with our sample.
[14:10] Marcus: ok that's great — we'll file that as high-priority investigation item.
[14:30] Rohit: another infra question — if on-prem, is the fallback routing still supported within a private cluster or do you require public control plane?
[14:38] Lena: Redwood Private offers local control plane and can run fallback policies within the VPC; the only caveat is for multi-region fallbacks you need peered networking.
[14:55] Rohit: noted. KMS key wrapping — do you store any plain keys?
[15:00] Marcus: no, Redwood Private can be configured so keys never leave your HSM. we store wrapped keys and we support HSM-based signing.
[15:20] Jia: i'll capture the required runbook steps for the dry-run and share.
[15:30] Marcus: quick note on metrics: we'll add a fallback_rate metric and correlate with model-variant and driver version.
[15:45] Ava: please include the token-level cost delta per prompt-class so our finance team can model spend.
[15:55] Lena: will include in the pricing update.
[16:14] Marcus: ok, i'm going to summarize the perf deltas we observed — INT8: median latency down 24%, cost down ~28%, rare quality outliers mostly in long-context/code. FP8: median latency down 30% but instability ~0.2-0.4% causing autoswitches. Impact on tail latency when fallback occurs is 200-800 ms depending on cache.
[16:55] Sofia: can you tag runs with commit and kernel versions so we can track if future upstream kernel patches address the instability?
[17:02] Marcus: yes every run is commit-tagged and we will include driver/cuda/kernel headers in the CSV.
[17:25] Rohit: about the sample size — can we increase to 10k synthetic prompts to reduce noise?
[17:30] Marcus: we can, but costs rise; let's do 1k targeted plus a 10k passive run overnight.
[17:45] Ava: for the 1k targeted, pick worst-affected prompt-classes: codegen, long-summarize, math chains.
[17:55] Marcus: noted.
[18:10] Jia: back to contractual items — pilot extension clause and SLAs?
[18:15] Lena: we'll propose a 30-day pilot with optional 30-day extension; dedicated pricing stub to follow.
[18:28] Sofia: we might also want an opt-out on FP8 promotion if instability persists.
[18:35] Lena: that's reasonable — we'll include a safe-promote clause.
[18:50] Marcus: last technical item — tokenizer pin and repro script will be in the repo, will include instructions to run parity tests.
[19:05] Ava: fantastic. also, can we get a sample audit log entry to validate your retention format (we have compliance to check)?
[19:12] Jia: yes i'll export a sanitized sample.
[19:22] Rohit: final infra ask — can we get a dry-run checklist for on-prem: driver versions, node configs, HSM test vectors, network ports?
[19:30] Marcus: i'll assemble a checklist and share in the runbook.
[19:42] Lena: ok let's close with a quick recap of owners and due dates.
[19:50] Lena: Marcus runs 1k regression + overnight 10k passive, due 11/18.
[19:57] Marcus: yep.
[20:00] Lena: Lena sends pricing and pilot stub 11/14. Jia creates dashboard and sample audit log 11/19, Rohit shares KMS/HSM docs 11/20.
[20:12] Ava: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[20:25] Lena: thanks folks — we'll follow up in email with links.
[20:30] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: middle segments have minor ASR mistakes (e.g., 'kay-vee cache' heard as "K V cache", 'fp8' sometimes transcribed as 'f p eight'), speaker labels occasionally merged.

References shared during call:
- Shared drive: /redwood/pilots/lumencloud/quant-2025-11 (Marcus will upload CSVs)
- Pricing sheet link: (placeholder) — Lena to send updated sheet

End of transcript.
